subject: alpine swift
title: How Does a Bird Stay in the Air for 200 Days Straight?

scenes.text: How does a bird live six months without landing?
Alpine swifts weigh less than a quarter of a pound. Yet tags showed three of them flying over 200 days straight.
They crossed to West Africa and stayed up there, day and night, eating insects caught in mid-air.
Sometimes they glided for minutes without a single flap.
How they sleep up there is still unexplained. Scientists think they may rest on the wing.
Six months in the sky. The ground was optional.

description:
Alpine swifts were tracked flying for more than 200 days in a row.
Small sensors recorded light and acceleration, and the data showed the birds staying airborne over West Africa, day and night, eating insects in flight.
The tags sampled every four minutes, so very brief landings cannot be ruled out.
Could you go a week without sitting down? Tell us below.
first_comment: The tags only checked every four minutes, so we can't rule out a quick landing, but no one has ever seen a swift rest in the air. How do YOU think it sleeps up there?
